input: Research freight forwarding for my online shop

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Freight forwarding covers many services (customs brokerage, warehousing, last-mile delivery, etc.) — knowing which are in scope prevents wasted research.
Whether the user is researching alone, presenting findings to partners/investors, or handing off to a logistics manager changes the depth and format needed.
The shipping routes (domestic, international, specific countries) fundamentally change which freight forwarders are relevant and what regulations apply.
Budget for freight costs or forwarder fees sets the tier of service that is realistic and which providers to shortlist.
Whether the user prioritises speed, cost, reliability, or sustainability will determine how to evaluate and rank forwarders.
Knowing what a good outcome looks like — a shortlist, a signed contract, an internal report — defines when the research task is actually done.
The type of goods (size, weight, fragility, hazardous classification) directly determines which freight modes and forwarders are even eligible.

gold.taskTitle: Research freight forwarding for your online shop
gold.taskDescription: Investigate freight forwarding options to support the shipping and logistics needs of an online retail business.

questions.title: Which freight forwarding services do you need to research?
questions.description: Clarify which specific services are in scope — e.g. customs brokerage, sea/air freight, warehousing, last-mile delivery — so research stays focused.

questions.title: Which countries or trade routes will you be shipping on?
questions.description: Identify the specific origin and destination countries or corridors, as this determines which forwarders are relevant and what regulations apply.

questions.title: What type of products will you be shipping?
questions.description: Establish the nature of the goods — dimensions, weight, fragility, or hazardous status — since this affects eligible freight modes and forwarder requirements.

questions.title: What is your monthly shipping volume or budget for freight?
questions.description: Understand the scale and financial envelope of the operation so that only realistic, appropriately sized forwarders are considered.

questions.title: What matters most: cost, speed, reliability, or sustainability?
questions.description: Pin down the primary evaluation criterion so that forwarders can be ranked meaningfully rather than compared on everything equally.

questions.title: Who will use the results of this research?
questions.description: Determine whether findings are for personal decision-making, a business partner, an investor pitch, or a logistics team, as this shapes the required depth and format.

questions.title: What does a completed research task look like to you?
questions.description: Define the tangible output — a shortlist of providers, a comparison table, a recommendation report, or a signed agreement — so there is a clear finish line.
